volume-8-s1: This volume uses four measures in supplementary material 3 from the Children and Families Agency: facilities, capacity, usage and waiting children. The prefectural column excludes separately listed designated and core cities. The report adds those 82 cities back to their prefectures to reconstruct all 47 regions. National totals reconcile for all four measures: 40,046 facilities, 3,016,417 places, 2,646,756 children using services and 2,435 waiting children.

Using only the left-hand table would understate prefectures containing major cities. Supplementary material 2’s municipal aggregation does not have exactly the same coverage as the summary. Its child counts were not combined with material 3’s capacity to calculate ratios; it was used only to identify the cities’ prefectures. Separate data-quality notes prevent later merging of incompatible scopes.

The report calculates utilisation as children using services divided by capacity. Capacity minus usage is an arithmetic difference, not bookable places. Previous-year waiting changes come from material 4 in the same release and are used only for that measure, not to infer earlier facilities or fees. The official release is provisional and subject to revision; every regional record retains that status.

The eight reading and chart groups are Hokkaido, Tohoku, Kanto, Chubu, Kinki, Chugoku, Shikoku, and Kyushu & Okinawa. Mie is included in Kinki. These groups do not define funding or legal jurisdictions.
volume-8-s2: Fifteen prefectures with the highest utilisation. Source: J01; prefectures reconstructed by the report. Children using services divided by capacity, not an education or safety score.
Fifteen prefectures with the largest childcare capacity. Source: J01; designated and core cities added back. Not total early childhood capacity.
Capacity and usage across 47 prefectures. Source: J01; calculated by the report. Point area varies with waiting children. Association does not establish causation.
Largest increases and decreases in waiting children. Source: J01, supplementary material 4. Only the waiting measure is compared; the chart alone does not establish causes.
Capacity and usage across eight regional groups. Source: J01; report grouping. Mie is in Kinki; Chugoku is the name of a Japanese geographic region.
Utilisation across all 47 prefectures. Source: J01; reconstructed and calculated by the report. Designated and core cities are included; figures are provisional.

These cross-sectional charts describe counts and ratios within one statistical population. More waiting children do not mean every service is poor; zero waiting does not remove eligibility, price, language or timing barriers. Utilisation is not classroom quality and cannot directly recommend local schools.
volume-8-s50: Prefectural totals describe structure, while applications and daily life operate at smaller scales. One prefecture may contain new housing areas with inward migration and shrinking communities. Subsidy rules, childcare applications and opening hours require local information, not just this volume’s totals.

Fix the measure before comparing places. Absolute waiting counts measure numbers; waiting rates need an application denominator; utilisation uses capacity; enrolment rates require child-population denominators. These ratios are not interchangeable. This report does not rename waiting divided by capacity an official waiting rate or use inconsistent age tables to infer births or coverage.
volume-8-s51: For updates, first establish the national release version, revision notes and reference date. Replace original values, reconstruct separately listed cities, reconcile national totals and regenerate derived ratios and charts. Changing only the heading’s year is insufficient. Preserve zero, missing and provisional values separately so visual completeness does not change statistical meaning.

Regional pages can later add municipal plans, local fees, facility registers and inspection records, but unverified gaps must not be filled with guesses. These profiles provide consistently defined childcare provision for 47 prefectures, not an exhaustive account of every kindergarten, unlicensed service or local policy.

An aggregate difference cannot cancel families? actual shortfalls: location, age and eligibility mean they are not the same population.
